thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: HIGH kv-cache eviction rate detected in region us-west-az3 (service: inference-runtime). Threshold breached: eviction_rate > 25% for 2 minutes. Pager: P12345 fired.

pagerduty-bot: Incident triggered (P12345). Escalation policy: runtime-oncall -> sre-lead.

raj.kapoor: ack. I'm on it. Switching to incident channel.

alice.martin: @raj can you confirm customer-impact? I'm seeing increased 500s from hosted endpoints in us-west-az3 in Datadog.

raj.kapoor: Confirmed. Dashboard shows tail latency spike and 5xx rate up ~3x for models with large KV usage. Likely kv-cache thrashing causing cold-token regen.

tess.ng: Noted similar spike in dedicated pools for a few customers. Opening tickets for any proactive customer comms.

jordan.sre: Is autoscaling kicking in? I see recent pod evictions around 12:07 UTC. Node pressure looks suspicious.

raj.kapoor: Autoscale did try, but new pods failing readiness due to OOMs on kvcache process. Suspect mem leak or corrupt shard leading to repeated evictions.

oncall-ml: tagging in: could be a recent runtime change that modified shard prefetching. Any deploy in the last 30m?

alice.martin: Deploy logs: rollouts: inference-runtime-canary v2.3.8 -> v2.3.9 at 11:50 UTC in us-west-az3 only. Canary flagged for extended warmup.

raj.kapoor: good catch. Rollout probably introduced increased memory per shard. Immediate mitigation: stop further canary rollout to az3 and divert traffic. I'm going to initiate routing fallback to az1/az2 for affected model routes.

support-engine: Customer impact estimate: 18 active customers with degraded responses, 4 experiencing timeouts >5s. Raising severity to Sev2 and notifying affected accounts.

raj.kapoor: Running failover command now.

raj.kapoor: ```
# route fallback to other zones for models with kvcache dependency
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routes/fallback" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"from_region":"us-west-az3","to_regions":["us-west-az1","us-west-az2"],"routes":["/v1/generate","/v1/chat"]}'
```

incident-bot: Routing fallback request accepted (req_id: fb-9876). Policy: gradual shift, 50% traffic over 3 min.

alice.martin: Monitoring: saw 40% of traffic shift within 2 minutes, 90% by 6 minutes. Error-rate on az3 dropping but still some residual 500s from in-flight sessions.

tess.ng: Can we scale az3 nodes down for now to prevent further evictions and preserve cluster health? Or cordon?

jordan.sre: I recommend cordoning affected nodes and draining. Will run a soft drain to avoid abrupt session loss. Command: `kubectl cordon node/az3-runtime-12 && kubectl drain node/az3-runtime-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30`

raj.kapoor: Running soft drain across 3 nodes. Also rolling back canary in az3 to v2.3.8. Initiating rollback.

oncall-ml: Meanwhile, capturing heap and kvcache stats for postmortem. Please save the following: `/var/log/runtime/kvcache-stats.log` and `pprof` snapshot.

support-engine: Sent initial customer comms to impacted accounts: "We are experiencing degraded performance in us-west-az3; traffic is being routed to healthy zones. No data loss. ETA for full recovery TBD."

alice.martin: After rollback and drains, we see eviction rate down to 4% and 5xx back to baseline on az3 for the last 3 min. Latency normalized.

pagerduty-bot: Incident P12345 acknowledged by raj.kapoor. Status: mitigated.

raj.kapoor: Marking incident mitigated. Keeping channel open for monitoring and follow-up. We'll keep the rollback in place and pause canary.

jordan.sre: I'll run a scheduled reconciliation to reintroduce capacity once we validate memory behavior over 1 hour. Also capturing node-level dmesg for OOM kills.

oncall-ml: Collected heap dumps and kvcache histograms. Preliminary look shows increased resident set size in the kvcache allocator after v2.3.9. Suspect allocator change.

tess.ng: Assigning postmortem: owners: alice.martin (runtime), raj.kapoor (oncall/troubleshooting), oncall-ml (analysis). Timeline and mitigations due EOD.

support-engine: Customer update: follow-up email sent — we routed traffic and rolled back the change; monitoring continues.

alice.martin: Thanks team. Quick notes: action items - 1) block v2.3.9 rollout across regions; 2) run extended soak in staging with large kv workloads; 3) add eviction alarms earlier (lower threshold).

raj.kapoor: I'll close PagerDuty after stable for 30m. Leaving channel open until then. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty P12345 status: mitigated -> awaiting close (30m silence).

support-engine: Adding a follow-up thread for postmortem doc and customer impact numbers.

alice.martin: Closing note: root cause likely runtime allocator change in v2.3.9 causing memory inflation per shard under heavy kv cache usage; verification and fix prioritized.

raj.kapoor: resolved for now. Will update when postmortem is ready.
